preamble: IgA Nephropathy  |  100-Point Adverse Prognostic Score  |  KDIGO 2021 Glomerular Disease Guidelines / IgAN Risk Prediction Tool (IgAN-RPT) / Oxford MEST-C Score  |  Progression Trajectory: Fast / Moderate / Slow

questions.question: Is time-averaged proteinuria >1 g/day (urine PCR >1.0 mg/mg) over ≥6 months of follow-up?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — sustained high-grade proteinuria confirmed; strongest independent predictor of ESRD in IgAN

questions.question: Is proteinuria >0.5 g/day despite ≥3 months of optimized RAS blockade (ACE inhibitor or ARB at maximum tolerated dose)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — proteinuria not controlled on optimal RAS therapy; high-risk marker; add-on therapy indicated

questions.question: Has proteinuria increased ≥50% from baseline on serial measurements over ≥6 months?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — rising proteinuria trajectory; disease not in remission; treatment escalation required

questions.question: Is eGFR <45 mL/min/1.73m² (CKD Stage 3b or worse) at presentation or follow-up?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — significantly reduced eGFR; IgAN patients with eGFR <45 have 5-year ESRD risk >30%

questions.question: Is annualized eGFR decline >3 mL/min/1.73m²/year on serial measurements over ≥12 months?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — progressive CKD trajectory confirmed; below median IgAN decline rate; high ESRD risk

questions.question: Is there significant tubular atrophy/interstitial fibrosis (Oxford T1: 26–50% or T2: >50% of cortical area)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — Oxford T1 or T2 confirmed; tubular atrophy is the strongest histologic predictor of ESRD in IgAN

questions.question: Is there mesangial hypercellularity (Oxford M1: >50% of glomeruli with mesangial score >2)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — Oxford M1 confirmed; active mesangial proliferation indicating ongoing immune injury

questions.question: Are crescents present (Oxford C1: ≥1 crescent in <25%; C2: crescents in ≥25% of glomeruli)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — crescentic IgAN confirmed; associated with rapid GFR decline; immunosuppression indicated

questions.question: Is systolic BP persistently ≥130 mmHg despite antihypertensive therapy including RAS blockade?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — uncontrolled hypertension confirmed; major modifiable progression driver in IgAN; target <120 mmHg per 2024 KDIGO

questions.question: Is galactose-deficient IgA1 (Gd-IgA1) elevated on serum testing? (elevated in ~60–70% of IgAN)
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — elevated Gd-IgA1 confirmed; underlying pathogenic mechanism active; predicts disease severity

questions.question: Is microscopic hematuria persistent on serial urinalysis (≥3 RBC/HPF on ≥3 separate UA reports over ≥12 months)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — persistent glomerular hematuria; correlates with ongoing endocapillary proliferation and disease activity

questions.question: Is the patient male with early-onset disease (<25 years), nephrotic-range proteinuria at presentation, or hypertension at diagnosis?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — multiple baseline high-risk features confirmed; cumulative risk substantially elevated above IgAN average
